E-020 and E-021 remain separate because creating a Sales Credit Note and applying a Customer Credit Note across Invoices are different permissions.

E-022 and E-023 remain separate because a signed Delivery Note photo and a goods photo apply under different delivery conditions.

E-045 and E-046 remain separate because overdue-Invoice and near-expiry alerts use different information, schedules and recipients.

E-064 to E-067 remain separate because Sales Order, Delivery Note, Invoice and Payment Receipt write-backs require separate field and direction decisions.

No earlier requirement was silently deleted. Prior items supported only by internal interpretation were moved to **Unsure**, **Decisions Required** or **Items Missing from the Latest Scope Lock**.

No final MAIA notification channel is confirmed; current operations use WhatsApp and UAT used Telegram.\
**10. Warnings and stops:** Invoice quantity above Delivery Note quantity and duplicate Invoice prevention were stated by the client. Credit warning versus complete stop and price-exception behaviour remain unresolved.\

**12. Existing-system sync:** SQL is the existing system. Customer and item information flow from SQL to MAIA. Proposed confirmed Sales Order, Delivery Note, Invoice and Payment Receipt updates flow from MAIA to SQL. Goods Receipt remains in SQL. No client-specific unit, warehouse or category translation table was found.\
**13. One-off or passing requests:** Recurring Wednesday orders, company-name lock, Pro Forma Invoice, Friday Statement of Account, address search, related-company pricing and customer complaint recording appeared once or mainly in later discussions.\
**14. Later changes:** Later evidence moved Sales toward own-order entry, added individual piece and box-weight handling, made notifications more important, proposed a Driver role, and exposed unresolved credit, Packing List and account-model decisions.

**1. Configuration Summary**

Macro Frozen needs at least seven named MAIA accounts, but the final account count cannot be set until warehouse, driver and backup access is decided.

David maintains Macro Frozen\'s selling prices; the exact people who may approve each price and credit exception remain partly unresolved.

Salespeople work with customers assigned through SQL agent codes, while default and former-agent customers belong to David.

Grace directly confirmed manual payment matching, cash handling and Credit Note work; the proposed automated payment flow must still prove that it reduces rather than repeats her work.

Lai owns the Pick List activity, but the account model, backup user, draft Delivery Note authority and final-quantity owner remain unresolved.

Macro Frozen uses actual weights and may receive orders in kilograms, cartons or pieces; the final digital method for individual box weights is not confirmed.

Notification recipients were discussed, but no final channel is confirmed. WhatsApp is the current operating channel and Telegram was used during UAT.

SQL remains the existing business system. Customer assignment is directly supported; document write-back fields and translation rules are not fully evidenced.

**2. Users and Roles**

**DAVID --- OWNER AND PRICE MAINTAINER**

David coordinates Macro Frozen and directly described how prices are maintained and how unassigned customers should be handled.

**Can**

**ROLE-01 --- Maintain the Item Price and Price List**

David can change the Item Price and Price List when Macro Frozen decides that a market price has risen or fallen.

Macro Frozen currently distributes price changes outside SQL, so one named person must control the current price used by Sales.

**Applies to:** Item Price; Price List\
**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026; Macrofrozen Client Scope Lock Clarification, 13 Jul 2026\
**Evidence:** E-010 (quoted), E-011 (quoted), E-037 (quoted)

**ROLE-02 --- Own customers without a current salesperson**

David can view and maintain a Customer when its SQL agent code is blank, default or belongs to a former salesperson.

Macro Frozen needs those customers to remain visible instead of becoming ownerless.

**Applies to:** Customer\
**Source:** Macrofrozen Client Scope Lock Clarification, 13 Jul 2026\
**Evidence:** E-031 (quoted), E-032 (quoted)

**Cannot**

*No restriction was evidenced for this role.*

**Unsure**

**ROLE-03 --- Approve a price below the minimum**

David is expected to decide a requested price below the minimum on the Quotation, Sales Order and Invoice, but the direct client evidence does not name those three document permissions.

**Decision needed:** May David approve below-minimum prices on the Quotation, Sales Order and Invoice?

The permission cannot be configured safely from a general minimum-price statement alone.

**Applies to:** Quotation; Sales Order; Invoice\
**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026; Scope Lock v3\
**Evidence:** E-013 (quoted)

**ROLE-04 --- Release a credit-blocked document**

David is described in later UAT material as the final credit decision-maker, but the client evidence also discusses CJ and Apple.

**Decision needed:** May David release a blocked Sales Order and a blocked Delivery Note?

The final credit authority is required before role permissions and notifications can be configured.

**Applies to:** Sales Order; Delivery Note\
**Source:** Macrofrozen 2nd UAT, 28 Jul 2026; Scope Lock v3\
**Evidence:** E-016 (quoted), E-017 (quoted)

**ROLE-05 --- Manage users and roles**

David was discussed as one of two administrators, but the client requested that administrator setup be reviewed again.

**Decision needed:** Does David hold system-administration permission to create, disable and change MAIA users and roles?

System administration must not be inferred from ownership of the business.

**Applies to:** User and role settings\
**Source:** Macrofrozen Client Scope Lock Clarification, 13 Jul 2026\
**Evidence:** E-025 (quoted), E-080 (derived)

**Suggested**

After the final credit authority is confirmed, name one temporary substitute who can receive only the price and credit permissions needed during David\'s recorded absence. This closes the no-backup gap without granting permanent Administrator access.

***This is a suggestion, not a confirmed client requirement.***

**Applies to:** Pick List; Delivery Note\

**Evidence:** E-041 (quoted)

**Suggested**

Configure Lai\'s eventual backup with time-limited Pick List and draft Delivery Note access rather than permanent Administrator access. This closes the absence gap while limiting unnecessary permissions.

***This is a suggestion, not a confirmed client requirement.***

**3. Notifications and Reminders**

A notification is sent because something happened and someone else needs to know or act; a message shown because the user\'s own action is blocked belongs under Warnings and Blocking Rules.

**Trigger type:** Schedule or condition --- exact schedule not confirmed\
**Channel:** Not confirmed

**When it is sent:** When an Invoice exceeds the agreed overdue threshold.

**Who receives it:** David, Finance, the assigned Salesperson and CJ for Ben or Arben and Queenie\'s customers.

**What they receive:** The overdue Invoice and Customer.

**Why they need it:** The client said the owner, Finance and Sales need to know who has not paid.

**What they do next:** Finance follows collection; the assigned Salesperson contacts the Customer; David and CJ review exposure.

**Unsure:** The overdue threshold, schedule, exact Finance recipient and final channel are not confirmed.

**Source:** Macrofrozen Client Scope Lock Clarification, 13 Jul 2026\

**4. Warnings and Blocking Rules**

**RULE-01 --- Salesperson cannot change Customer credit limit**

**What the user is trying to do:** CJ, Ben or Arben, or Queenie is trying to change the credit limit on a Customer.

**When MAIA intervenes:** The account is using ordinary Salesperson permission.

**What MAIA does:** MAIA stops the change and leaves the credit limit read-only.

**What MAIA tells the user:** The credit limit can be read but cannot be changed with Salesperson permission.

**What happens next:** The named credit-limit owner changes the Customer credit limit after DECISION-03 is answered.

**Why this rule is needed:** The client directly separated Sales reading from credit-limit maintenance.

**Applies to:** Customer credit limit.

**Source:** Macrofrozen Client Scope Lock Clarification, 13 Jul 2026\
**Evidence:** E-028 (quoted)

**RULE-02 --- Customer access outside the assigned salesperson**

**Unsure**

The SQL agent code identifies the salesperson who owns a Customer, but the reviewed client words do not explicitly say MAIA must stop another Salesperson from viewing that Customer.

**Decision needed:** Must MAIA stop CJ, Ben or Arben, and Queenie from viewing a Customer assigned to another salesperson?

**Product confirmation needed:** It is unclear whether this is standard MAIA behaviour or requires a client-specific configuration.

**Applies to:** Customer.

**Source:** Macrofrozen Client Scope Lock Clarification, 13 Jul 2026\
**Evidence:** E-030 (quoted), E-032 (quoted)

**RULE-03 --- Unclear payment match requires Grace**

**What the user is trying to do:** Grace is trying to apply a Payment Receipt to an Invoice.

**When MAIA intervenes:** The payer name does not identify one clear Customer.

**What MAIA does:** MAIA requires Grace to select the Customer before the Payment Receipt changes an Invoice balance.

**What MAIA tells the user:** The payer name does not match one clear Customer and Finance must select the correct Customer.

**What happens next:** Grace selects the Customer and then selects the Invoice or Invoices.

**Why this rule is needed:** Macro Frozen receives payments from names that may differ from the Customer record.

**Applies to:** Payment Receipt; Invoice.

**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026\
**Evidence:** E-006 (quoted), E-007 (quoted)

**RULE-04 --- Price outside the approved boundary**

**Unsure**

Macro Frozen directly stated that it uses minimum, maximum and fixed prices, but the reviewed direct client evidence does not define the result on each document.

**Decision needed:** What must MAIA do when a Salesperson enters a price below the minimum on a Quotation?

Separate decisions are also required for the Sales Order and Invoice; they are listed independently in Section 6 to avoid one question covering several documents.

**Applies to:** Quotation.

**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026\
**Evidence:** E-013 (quoted)

**RULE-05 --- Invoice quantity above Delivery Note quantity**

**What the user is trying to do:** Grace is trying to submit an Invoice with a quantity greater than the related Delivery Note quantity.

**When MAIA intervenes:** The Invoice quantity exceeds the Delivery Note quantity.

**What MAIA does:** MAIA stops submission and requires the Invoice quantity to be corrected.

**What MAIA tells the user:** The Invoice quantity cannot exceed the delivered quantity.

**What happens next:** Grace corrects the Invoice quantity and submits it again.

**Why this rule is needed:** Macro Frozen does not want to bill more than it delivered.

**Applies to:** Delivery Note; Invoice.

**Product confirmation needed:** It is unclear whether this is standard MAIA behaviour or requires a client-specific configuration.

**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026\
**Evidence:** E-018 (quoted)

**RULE-06 --- Duplicate Invoice**

**Unsure**

Macro Frozen directly described the risk of creating another Invoice for the same transaction, but the exact duplicate condition was not defined.

**Decision needed:** Which existing document relationship makes a new Invoice a duplicate?

**Product confirmation needed:** It is unclear whether this is standard MAIA behaviour or requires a client-specific configuration.

**Applies to:** Invoice.

**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026\
**Evidence:** E-019 (quoted)

**RULE-07 --- Credit check on Sales Order**

**Unsure**

The client described previous-Invoice payment discipline and a one-time exception, but the calculation and warn-versus-stop result remain unresolved.

**Decision needed:** Does a failed credit check stop the Sales Order from being submitted?

**Applies to:** Sales Order.

**Source:** Macrofood Requirements Gathering transcript v2, 4 Jun 2026; Scope Lock v3\
**Evidence:** E-016 (quoted), E-017 (quoted)

**RULE-08 --- Warehouse cost and Purchasing visibility**

**Unsure**

Internal Product discussion says Lai and Warehouse Workers should not see buying cost, item value or Purchasing information, but no direct client quotation was located.

**Decision needed:** Must MAIA hide buying cost, item value and Purchasing information from Lai and Warehouse Workers?

**Applies to:** Item; Purchasing information.

**Source:** Product Scope Gap Brief, 24 Jul 2026\
**Evidence:** E-069 (derived)

**Suggested**

No client-specific suggestion identified for this section. The unresolved client rules must be decided before adding another warning or stop.

**AUTO-12 --- Keep Goods Receipt in SQL and use SQL stock**

**Unsure**

**When it happens:** When supplier goods are received and when MAIA needs the latest stock level.

**What MAIA does:** Macro Frozen continues supplier Goods Receipt in SQL; MAIA uses the available stock information from SQL.

**Suggested**

When a Customer or Item from SQL cannot be matched during AUTO-03 or AUTO-11, leave the document in draft with the unmatched original value visible and assign it to the person who initiated the action. This closes the silent-mapping failure path without inventing a Customer, Item or code.

***This is a suggestion, not a confirmed client requirement.***

**6. Decisions Required**

**Blocking --- configuration cannot proceed**

**DECISION-01 --- System administrator**

**Question:** Does Apple hold system-administration permission to create, disable and change MAIA users and roles?

**Why it must be answered:** Administrator access is broad and the client explicitly requested reconfirmation.

**Who should decide:** David

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-05, ROLE-28

**Evidence on each side:** E-025 (quoted) names David and Apple; E-080 (derived) identifies the required administration function.

**DECISION-02 --- David system administration**

**Question:** Does David hold system-administration permission to create, disable and change MAIA users and roles?

**Why it must be answered:** Ownership of the company does not automatically prove a system-administrator permission.

**Who should decide:** David

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-05

**Evidence on each side:** E-025 (quoted) names David during the administrator discussion, but the arrangement was not final.

**DECISION-03 --- Customer credit-limit owner**

**Question:** May Apple create or change a Customer credit limit?

**Why it must be answered:** The field owner is unresolved between Apple and CJ.

**Who should decide:** David with Grace

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-10, ROLE-29

**Evidence on each side:** E-028 (quoted) says Sales cannot change the limit; E-029 (quoted) discusses Sales Manager involvement without a final answer.

**DECISION-04 --- Final credit approver**

**Question:** May David release a blocked Sales Order?

**Why it must be answered:** The Sales Order cannot be configured without a named person who may continue it.

**Who should decide:** David

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-04, NOTIF-05, RULE-07

**Evidence on each side:** E-016 (quoted) and E-017 (quoted) show payment discipline and one-time exception; the named approver is not directly confirmed.

**DECISION-05 --- Warehouse account model**

**Question:** Will warehouse workers use named individual accounts?

**Why it must be answered:** Individual accounts and a shared account create different permissions, counts and auditability.

**Who should decide:** David with Lai

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-36, ROLE-37

**Evidence on each side:** E-004 (quoted) asks for picker identity; E-040 (quoted) describes one shared phone.

**DECISION-06 --- Lai backup**

**Question:** Who receives Lai\'s Pick List and draft Delivery Note permissions during his absence?

**Why it must be answered:** No safe warehouse continuation exists without a named person.

**Who should decide:** David

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-35, NOTIF-03, NOTIF-04

**Evidence on each side:** E-041 (quoted) says nobody currently checks when Lai is absent.

**DECISION-07 --- Grace backup**

**Question:** Who receives Grace\'s Payment Receipt, Sales Credit Note, Customer Credit Note, Delivery Note and Invoice permissions during her absence?

**Why it must be answered:** Finance work cannot be assigned to an unnamed "boss\'s wife."

**Who should decide:** David with Grace

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-19--ROLE-27

**Evidence on each side:** E-042 (quoted) describes current backup practice without a name or MAIA role.

**DECISION-08 --- Sales Order submission**

**Question:** May Ben or Arben submit a Sales Order after checking it?

**Why it must be answered:** The answer determines whether Sales has submit permission or requires CJ.

**Who should decide:** David with CJ

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-17

**Evidence on each side:** E-051 (derived) assigns own-order submission; no clean client quotation confirms it.

**DECISION-09 --- Final Delivery Note submission**

**Question:** May Grace submit the Delivery Note after Lai creates a draft?

**Why it must be answered:** The document has no confirmed final submit owner.

**Who should decide:** David with Grace and Lai

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-25, ROLE-32, NOTIF-04

**Evidence on each side:** E-053 (derived) and E-054 (derived) describe the proposed handoff.

**DECISION-10 --- Invoice permission**

**Question:** May Grace create and submit the Invoice after the Delivery Note is ready?

**Why it must be answered:** Invoice creation and submission cannot be inferred from Finance involvement alone.

**Who should decide:** David with Grace

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-26

**Evidence on each side:** E-055 (derived) describes the UAT role design.

**DECISION-11 --- Actual-quantity owner**

**Question:** May Lai amend the Sales Order to the accepted actual quantity after picking?

**Why it must be answered:** The final quantity controls the Delivery Note and Invoice.

**Who should decide:** David with Lai and Grace

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-34, AUTO-09

**Evidence on each side:** E-005 (quoted) confirms the weight difference; E-058 (derived) identifies the required update.

**DECISION-12 --- SQL Sales Order write-back**

**Question:** Which Sales Order fields are sent from MAIA to SQL?

**Why it must be answered:** The Sales Order update cannot be tested without a field list.

**Who should decide:** Product Owner with Macro Frozen and SQL provider

**Affected requirement IDs:** AUTO-11

**Evidence on each side:** E-064 (derived) identifies the proposed write-back; no field list was found.

**DECISION-13 --- SQL Delivery Note write-back**

**Question:** Which Delivery Note fields are sent from MAIA to SQL?

**Why it must be answered:** The Delivery Note update cannot be tested without a field list.

**Who should decide:** Product Owner with Macro Frozen and SQL provider

**Affected requirement IDs:** AUTO-11

**Evidence on each side:** E-065 (derived) identifies the proposed write-back; no field list was found.

**DECISION-14 --- SQL Invoice write-back**

**Question:** Which Invoice fields are sent from MAIA to SQL?

**Why it must be answered:** The Invoice update cannot be tested without a field list.

**Who should decide:** Product Owner with Macro Frozen and SQL provider

**Affected requirement IDs:** AUTO-11

**Question:** Which Payment Receipt fields are sent from MAIA to SQL?

**Who should decide:** Product Owner with Grace and SQL provider

**Affected requirement IDs:** AUTO-11

**Evidence on each side:** E-067 (derived) identifies the proposed write-back; no field list was found.

**Deferrable --- a default can be used and revisited**

**DECISION-16 --- Other-salesperson Customer visibility**

**Question:** Must MAIA stop Salespeople from viewing a Customer assigned to another salesperson?

**Why it must be answered:** Assignment is confirmed, but an explicit stop was not directly stated.

**Who should decide:** David with CJ

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-18, RULE-02

**Proposed default:** Use MAIA\'s standard Customer visibility with no extra client-specific restriction until the client answers.

**What changes if answered differently:** A "yes" answer requires a Customer visibility restriction by SQL agent code.

**Evidence on each side:** E-030 (quoted) and E-032 (quoted) establish assignment, not an explicit denial.

**DECISION-17 --- CJ customer approval**

**Question:** Must CJ approve a Customer created by a Salesperson?

**Why it must be answered:** Grace proposed the approval, but the role matrix was left for review.

**Who should decide:** David with CJ and Grace

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-08, ROLE-12

**Proposed default:** Allow Customer creation under the standard MAIA state but do not add a client-specific approval requirement before confirmation.

**What changes if answered differently:** A "yes" answer adds a manager decision after Customer creation.

**Evidence on each side:** E-027 (quoted) permits creation; E-029 (quoted) proposes manager approval.

**DECISION-18 --- CJ price permission**

**Question:** May CJ approve a reduced price on a Quotation when it remains at or above the minimum?

**Why it must be answered:** Later documents assign this permission without a clean direct client sentence.

**Who should decide:** David

**Affected requirement IDs:** ROLE-09, NOTIF-06

**Proposed default:** Do not grant CJ a new client-specific Quotation price permission until confirmed.

**What changes if answered differently:** A "yes" answer grants CJ the stated Quotation permission and routes NOTIF-06 to him for that condition.

**Evidence on each side:** E-013 (quoted) confirms price boundaries; the named CJ permission is derived.

**DECISION-19 --- Sales Order credit result**

**Question:** Does a failed credit check stop the Sales Order from being submitted?

**Why it must be answered:** The client described discipline and exceptions but not the final result.

**Who should decide:** David with Grace

**Affected requirement IDs:** RULE-07, NOTIF-05

**Proposed default:** Leave the standard MAIA credit behaviour unchanged and do not add a Macro Frozen-specific stop until confirmed.

**What changes if answered differently:** A "yes" answer adds a complete stop and approval request; a "no" answer requires a separate warning decision.

**Evidence on each side:** E-016 (quoted) and E-017 (quoted) support the business rule.

**DECISION-20 --- Quotation below-minimum behaviour**

**Question:** What must MAIA do when a Salesperson enters a price below the minimum on a Quotation?

**Why it must be answered:** The client named the boundary but not the intervention.

**Who should decide:** David

**Affected requirement IDs:** RULE-04, NOTIF-06

**Proposed default:** Leave the standard MAIA Quotation behaviour unchanged and do not add a client-specific intervention.

**What changes if answered differently:** The client answer may add correction, stop or approval behaviour.

**Evidence on each side:** E-013 (quoted) confirms minimum price.

**DECISION-21 --- Near-expiry threshold**

**Question:** How many days before expiry trigger NOTIF-02?

**Why it must be answered:** The alert cannot identify qualifying stock without a number.

**Who should decide:** David with Lai

**Affected requirement IDs:** NOTIF-02

**Proposed default:** Keep the client-specific near-expiry alert disabled until the threshold and expiry-data source are confirmed.

**What changes if answered differently:** A confirmed number enables the alert for qualifying stock.

**Evidence on each side:** E-046 (quoted) confirms recipients; E-047 (quoted) says expiry tracking is future-facing.

**DECISION-22 --- Overdue-Invoice threshold**

**Question:** How many overdue days trigger NOTIF-01?

**Why it must be answered:** The alert cannot run without a threshold.

**Who should decide:** David with Grace

**Affected requirement IDs:** NOTIF-01

**Proposed default:** Keep the client-specific overdue-Invoice alert disabled until the threshold is confirmed.

**What changes if answered differently:** A confirmed number enables the scheduled or condition-based alert.

**Evidence on each side:** E-045 (quoted) confirms the recipient groups.

**DECISION-23 --- Notification channel**

**Question:** Does NOTIF-03 arrive through WhatsApp?

**Why it must be answered:** Current work uses WhatsApp, UAT used Telegram and MAIA channel was not locked.

**Who should decide:** David with Lai and Product

**Affected requirement IDs:** NOTIF-03

**Proposed default:** Use only standard in-app notification behaviour and do not attach a PDF until Product and the client confirm the channel.

**What changes if answered differently:** A "yes" answer requires WhatsApp delivery and a Product decision on PDF attachment support.

**Evidence on each side:** E-001 (quoted) confirms WhatsApp orders; E-052 (derived) defines the proposed notification.

**DECISION-24 --- Friday Statement of Account**

**Question:** Does MAIA automatically send the Statement of Account every Friday?

**Why it must be answered:** The direct sentence confirms the Friday activity but not automation.

**Who should decide:** Grace

**Affected requirement IDs:** NOTIF-07, MISSING-07

**Proposed default:** Leave the Statement of Account as a manual Finance activity outside client-specific automation.

**What changes if answered differently:** A "yes" answer requires recipient, time, channel and document-generation details.

**Evidence on each side:** E-073 (quoted) confirms the Friday cycle.
